answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a prism-and-wharf trust model. Every new identity docks as a vertex at the wharf and must finish bonded work—reviews, triage, escrow—before its vertex earns edges. Reputation flows like light through a prism: attestations refract into contribution spectra. A Sybil farm emits a narrow single-band burst of mutual praise, a low-entropy signature honest clusters never show; real vertices scatter across spectra. The wharf taxes each fake with labor, prismatic entropy exposes the farm, and idle docking rights decay, so phantom fleets rot at anchor.
